title: Handoffs and Shared State
brief: A sales agent closes three upgrades, then hands each customer to a support agent to finish setup. Right now the handoff passes the whole sales conversation: about 9,000 tokens of pitch, pricing tool output and small talk. The support agent pays to read all of it and sometimes keeps selling. Get at least 85% of setups right while support's context stays under 5,000 tokens.

handoff_full.text: transfer_to_support(history=ALL) → support receives the full sales conversation: 41 messages, pricing tool output, the pitch deck summary

handoff_summary.text: transfer_to_support(note="Customer upgraded, please finish setup.") → support receives a one-line free-text summary

handoff_record.text: transfer_to_support(record={account, plan, seats, billing, promised_discount, sso, open_questions}) → support receives the structured handoff record plus the customer's last message

setup.text: update_account(plan, seats, billing, promised_terms, sso) with the values from the handoff, e.g. plan="Team", seats=40, billing="annual", discount=0.15

ask_again.text: Support to customer: 'Thanks for upgrading! Could you remind me which plan and how many seats you agreed on?' (The customer already told sales all of this.)

done_ok.text: You're all set: plan, seats and billing match what sales agreed, the promised terms are on your first invoice, and nothing is left open.

upsell.text: Setup is done! While you're here, have you considered the Enterprise add-on? (Support read the sales instructions in the transcript and kept pitching; one setup step was skipped.)

lost_detail.text: You're all set on your new plan. (The promise sales made, a discount, a free month or a new billing email, was not in the summary, so the first invoice is wrong.)

modifiers.note: With no shared state, the default handoff passes the whole conversation.
A thin summary forces support to ask the customer again.
Full transcript: support sees the sales prompt and keeps pitching about 1 time in 4.
Free-text summary: cheap, but details like the promised discount drop out.
Structured record: every field the setup needs is there by name.

goals.label: At least 85% of setups exactly as sold

hints: Read a failing setup. What did support receive, and which part of it led it astray?
Passing nothing loses the deal; passing everything passes the sales prompt too. Try a Memory node set to summary and see what drops out.
Use a Memory node of kind profile: a structured handoff record (plan, seats, billing, promised discount, SSO) that both agents read and write.
explain: A handoff is a contract between two agents. A structured record carries every field the next agent needs by name, costs a few hundred tokens, and leaves the sales prompt behind.
